title: Income Tax Act 2025: Crypto VDA Tax Rules, TDS & ITR Filing
description: The Income Tax Act, 2025 largely continues the existing tax framework for Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs). A flat 30% tax will still be levied on income from VD.

faq.q: What is a Virtual Digital Asset (VDA) under the Income Tax Act 2025?
faq.a: A Virtual Digital Asset (VDA) is defined broadly to include any information or code or number or token generated through cryptographic means or otherwise, providing a digital representation of value exchanged with or without consideration, with the promise or expectation of a utility, or interest, and includes NFTs and any other digital asset as the Central Government may specify.

faq.q: Has the 30% tax rate on VDA income changed?
faq.a: No, the Income Tax Act, 2025 largely retains the existing provision of a flat 30% tax rate on income derived from the transfer of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs).

faq.q: How does the 1% TDS on VDA transactions operate?
faq.a: A 1% Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) is applicable on the consideration paid for the transfer of a VDA, provided the transaction value exceeds certain thresholds (₹50,000 for specified persons, ₹10,000 for others). This TDS is deducted by the buyer or the VDA exchange and can be claimed as a credit against your final tax liability.

faq.q: Can I adjust VDA losses against other income or VDA gains?
faq.a: No, the Income Tax Act, 2025 continues to prohibit the set-off of losses arising from the transfer of Virtual Digital Assets against any other income or even against gains from other VDA transfers. Such losses cannot be carried forward to subsequent assessment years either.

faq.q: What specific records must I maintain for VDA transactions?
faq.a: You must maintain detailed records including the date, time, type of VDA, quantity, value in INR, transaction ID/hash, wallet addresses (sender/receiver), exchange details, and any associated fees for every VDA transaction.

faq.q: Will the ITR filing process for VDAs be different?
faq.a: While the core tax rules remain, the new reporting framework under the Income Tax Act, 2025 will likely require more detailed disclosure of VDA transactions within your Income Tax Return (ITR). You should anticipate specific schedules or enhanced sections dedicated to reporting VDA income and TDS.
